issues.description: The trace_pairs.json file is not valid bare JSON. It contains a large block of prose/reasoning text (the author's scratch-work narrative about how to construct the traces) before the actual JSON object begins. This causes json.loads() to fail with 'Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)', which is exactly the error observed in the differential test run.
issues.evidence: golden_run stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: SR3: independent DFA cross-check failed to run: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'

issues.description: Because trace_pairs.json fails to parse, SR3 fails even for the golden/expert-correct submission. The differential test confirms golden_run status=fail when expected=pass. This means a fully correct participant submission would be rejected by the grader, violating the core requirement that a correct answer passes.

The manifest purpose statement for this file claims it was 'FIXED per repair notes' to be strictly valid bare JSON with zero surrounding content, but the actual shipped file content still contains the full narrative preamble. The repair was described but not actually applied to the artifact.
issues.evidence: manifest purpose: 'must be a single bare, strictly valid JSON document parseable by json.loads() with ZERO surrounding content -- no leading prose/reasoning narrative' vs actual file content beginning with 'I need to construct trace pairs where key[3:0]=0xA...'

issues.description: requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0 and mutation_status is blocked_by_differential, confirming the benchmark cannot currently be used to discriminate correct from incorrect submissions due to the SR3/trace_pairs.json defect.

recommendations: Regenerate inputs/trace_pairs.json to contain ONLY the bare JSON object (the {"traces": [...]} structure), stripping out all of the preceding narrative/reasoning text so that json.loads() succeeds.
Re-run the differential test after the fix to confirm the golden submission now passes all of FR1-FR4 and SR1-SR4 (exit code 0) and the baseline submission still fails at least SR1/SR2/SR3/SR4/FR4.

Add a CI/lint check (e.g. a simple python -c "import json; json.load(open('inputs/trace_pairs.json'))" step) to the artifact-generation pipeline to catch this class of malformed-JSON regression before shipping.

Consider using the existing tests/private/regen_trace_pairs.py generator to deterministically regenerate a clean trace_pairs.json and verify byte-for-byte that inputs/trace_pairs.json matches its output.

requirement_results.evidence: Golden and baseline both correctly evaluated for FR1 in differential run.
Golden PASS FR2; baseline PASS FR2 (baseline has valid-range but wrong values, which is expected since FR2 only checks range).
Golden PASS FR3; baseline PASS FR3.
Golden PASS FR4; baseline correctly FAILS FR4 (only one entry).
Golden PASS SR1; baseline correctly FAILS SR1 ('key_reg' != 'state_q').
Golden PASS SR2; baseline correctly FAILS SR2.

Golden run FAILS SR3 due to trace_pairs.json parse error ('Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)'), meaning the correct/golden submission cannot pass overall. This breaks the fundamental pass/fail contract for the task.
requirement_results.requirement: SR3 (independent DFA cross-check of recovered subkey nibble)

requirement_results.evidence: Golden PASS SR4; baseline correctly FAILS SR4 (generic advice only).
